proposals.evidence: Propose ordered ten + six. DEDR3918 documents the patiṉ-/padn-/pon- combining forms of ten in these teens, and DEDR2485 gives āṟu/ār six and explicitly Toda pāṟ sixteen. The southern census variants retain contraction, p/h alternation and vowel notation; uncertain census lect labels remain source qualifications, not corrections.

proposals.evidence: Propose ordered four × ten. DEDR3655 and3918 explicitly give Tamil nāṟpatu/nāppatu, Malayalam nālpatu, Kannada nālvattu and Kota nālvat forty. Survey forms are comparative variants of these formations, preserving assimilation, reduced vowels and final vowels. No independent one-stem etymology is substituted for the two numeral components.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5373 gives vāḻai/vāḻa and Kannada bāḻe banana; DEDR4004 gives Irula pammu/pāmu and Kannada paṇṇu fruit. Survey vā-/vē-/bāḷa-/bē- plus pammu/pāmu/paṇṇu-type banana responses are proposed contracted banana + ripe-fruit compounds. The contractions are comparative analyses, preserving the original complete response, rather than separately attested dictionary headwords.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1173 supplies gaṇḍu/gaṇḍ male and DEDR4616 supplies maga/magu/mog child/person. Survey gaṇḍu-maka/kaṇḍu-muga/gaṇa-mage/gan-mug is an ordered male + child/person compound, with source cluster reduction and final vowels retained. This is a comparative component analysis, not a claim that the entire compound is an indivisible inherited stem.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4885 directly groups the mīn fish series in Kannada, Kodagu, Kota, Tamil, Tulu and Malto (mínu). The survey final -ə and Malto -du are retained. Badaga and Ravula are comparative extensions explicitly labelled look-alikes by the upstream annotation; neither is falsely described as listed in DEDR. The article’s Sanskrit mīna comparison does not itself specify a loan route for these records. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
